assumption_assessment.name: Quot.sound
assumption_assessment.exact_statement: axiom sound : ∀ {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {a b : α}, r a b → Quot.mk r a = Quot.mk r b
assumption_assessment.trust: Primitive quotient equality principle of the host proof theory, not an artifact-validation assumption. The host kernel and primitive implementation remain trusted.
assumption_assessment.dependency_evidence: Both exact imported reports include it. Intermediate quotient/extensionality proof edges were not reconstructed.
assumption_assessment.discharge: Keep as named background theory; reducing proof-specific dependence is a different proof-development task, not evidence that Lean or its kernel is sound.

assumption_assessment.name: Lean.Level.instLawfulBEqLevel
assumption_assessment.expanded_obligation: For the installed Level BEq: a == a is true, and a == b being true entails propositional a = b. Core lines 782–804 provide the class fields.
assumption_assessment.trust: RuntimeLevel lines 255–258 bind BEq to opaque Level.beq with extern lean_level_eq. This asserts structural/propositional equality correctness for all levels, which is stronger than merely preserving Nat evaluation. It does not establish correctness of the C++ implementation, cached representation, compiler or linked runtime.
assumption_assessment.dependency_evidence: Canonical CVC-1 E7 uses beq_iff_eq in core isEquiv_sound; VerifyLevel lines 3808–3815 and 3861–3864 invoke isEquiv_wf in the core fast path. The complete interior LevelStd theorem path was not reread under this six-file allocation. Raw reports establish the actual terminal dependency membership.
assumption_assessment.discharge: An explicit structural equality function with a proved LawfulBEq instance is a feasible design alternative; proving it refines the opaque extern still requires a runtime bridge. Neither the C++ source nor this equality-refinement proof was inspected or established. Removing the core fast path may avoid this particular branch dependency, but requires a new comparator contract and an exact future axiom audit.

assumption_assessment.name: Lean.Level.isExplicitSubsumedAux_eq
assumption_assessment.expanded_obligation: Extensional equality for every Array Level, maximum explicit Nat, and starting Nat index. The total function returns true upon finding an offset at least the threshold while advancing the index, and false after the array end.
assumption_assessment.trust: Axiom bridges an opaque partial helper to its total counterpart. RuntimeLevel 367–373 and Axioms 187–194 have corresponding branch/advance/end behavior. This is source-level consistency evidence, not a checked equality or source-to-binary result. Sorted-array intent in comments is not a premise of the axiom.
assumption_assessment.dependency_evidence: RuntimeLevel 375–404 places this helper inside isExplicitSubsumed and normalize; Axioms 196–257 supplies the total normalization copy and normalize_eq. Actual theorem membership is in both fixed reports. The intervening helper proof steps in LevelStd are not available in the allocated files and remain uninspected, so the algorithm call graph is not presented as a complete proof-term graph.
assumption_assessment.discharge: A future upstream totalization or a theorem establishing a suitable refinement for the partial implementation could remove the assumption. The bound decreases as the index advances toward array size, making totalization plausible. Replacing definitions in a fresh strategy can avoid opaque equality but cannot prove the old opaque constant equal by textual inspection alone.

assumption_assessment.name: Lean.Level.normalize_eq
assumption_assessment.trust: Extensional identity between a full opaque partial normalization algorithm and its total copy is a substantial implementation bridge. It is not an axiom of universe semantic preservation, but source-side clause correspondence alone does not discharge it or authenticate binary behavior.
assumption_assessment.dependency_evidence: Canonical CVC-1 E7 directly shows eval_normalize rewriting normalize_eq, then isEquiv_sound using eval_normalize. VerifyLevel wrappers retain the core branch. Axioms 196–253 contains the total copy and termination arguments.
assumption_assessment.discharge: Use a total implementation with checked semantic theorems, or establish a separately reviewed refinement to the original implementation. A pure Normalize strategy is a promising alternative but its full reduced closure is not printed here.

assumption_assessment.name: Std.TreeMap.all_eq_all_toList
assumption_assessment.exact_statement: axiom all_eq_all_toList {p : α → β → Bool} : t.all p = t.toList.all fun a => p a.1 a.2
assumption_assessment.implicit_context: {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {cmp : α → α → Ordering} {t : TreeMap α β cmp}
assumption_assessment.trust: Container traversal equivalence used to connect Boolean map checks with entry-wise reasoning. It does not assume semantic universe equivalence. The relevant map implementation was not inspected in this bounded review.
assumption_assessment.dependency_evidence: VerifyLevel NormLevel.eval_congr at 1273–1293 uses this axiom; isEquiv'_wf at 3815 invokes that result. NormLevel.le_eval at 1250 and later completeness machinery also use the bridge.
assumption_assessment.discharge: A proof against the exact map implementation or a list-based successor strategy could eliminate the helper axiom. Feasibility is plausible but unverified and not a reason to drop the present dependency.
